headline: FedEx 2027 GRI: 5.9% average; fourth straight 5.9% headline
details: Standard list rates for U.S., U.S. export, U.S. import package services: avg 5.9%; minimums and surcharges also rise Jan 4
AHS: $29.50-$40.75 rising to $31.75-$43.75 by zone (Logistics Management)
Residential delivery charge $6.95 to $7.35 (service not specified in source)
Analyses: 5 of 7 major services above 5.9%; Express Saver ~3.09%; Ground/Home Delivery ~6.1% avg zones 2-8
DAS and Pickup Area Surcharge ZIP lists change (FedEx rate tools page)
note: Announcement date not confirmed (one source says Sept 18, 2026; coverage late Sept 2026). Freight-specific % not found. Service-level % from consultancies.

headline: FedEx zone realignment between select U.S. ZIP codes
details: Zone reclassification for select ZIP pairs scheduled Feb 1, 2027
note: Affected ZIP pairs not identified; date mainly from a secondary timeline.

headline: FedEx adds $25 paper trade document fee and $5 manual airbill fee
details: $25 fee when a trade document is provided in non-electronic format
$5 fee for U.S. domestic and export shipments initiated with manual paper airbills
note: One trade source plus one secondary; announced with 2027 GRI.

headline: UPS 2027 GRI: 5.9% average for Ground, Air and International (Daily Rates), effective Dec 21, 2026
details: Daily Rates for UPS Ground, UPS Air and International: average net increase of 5.9%, effective Dec 21, 2026
Additional Handling minimum billable weight 40 -> 50 lb; Area Surcharge and zone ZIP lists change
New per-package surcharge on Ground and Ground Saver from certain origin ZIPs for Qualified customers (amount not stated)
UPS says detailed rate previews will follow; individual impact varies by shipping profile and UPS agreement
Small Business Rates change separately: +4.5% plus a new 5% fuel surcharge (entry ups-2027-sbr-2026-12-21)
note: Announced date: Oct 23, 2026 is when the notice was first found on UPS's Important Updates page (story w84705482dd2f, detected 2026-10-23, UTC). UPS's page prints no posting date, so it may have gone up late on Oct 22 U.S. time.

headline: UPS Small Business Rates: +4.5% plus a new 5% fuel surcharge from Dec 21, 2026
details: SBR rates rise 4.5%, effective Dec 21, 2026
A 5% fuel surcharge applies to all SBR shipments, domestic and international
About 9.7% combined (1.045 x 1.05) before agreement terms
The SBR page still advertises SBR rates as inclusive of Delivery Area Surcharge and Fuel Surcharge
Additional Handling minimum billable weight 40 -> 50 lb
note: From UPS's Small Business Rates page as checked on Oct 24, 2026. The page states no announcement date.

headline: 8% temporary increase and 2026 peak rates both expire Jan 17, 2027; no 2027 shipping filing yet
details: Both the April 2026 8% transportation increase and the 2026 peak surcharge end at midnight CT Jan 17, 2027 (USPS)
As of mid-October 2026, no USPS/PRC notice of a January 2027 shipping price change was found
PRC Order 9696 (Aug 21, 2026) denied USPS a waiver to use estimated data for extra market-dominant rate authority; USPS may still file in Oct 2026 for a January 2027 mail change
note: No announced 2027 shipping price figures exist in sources found (as of 2026-10-21). USPS has said it will decide whether a different long-term approach is needed after Jan 17, 2027. Re-check USPS newsroom/PRC for a late-October or November 2026 competitive filing.

headline: FedEx completes spin-off of FedEx Freight; FDXF begins trading on NYSE
details: Regular-way trading began June 1, 2026 under ticker FDXF
FedEx distributed 80.1% to shareholders and kept 19.9%, to dispose of within 24 months
John Smith is FedEx Freight president and CEO
why: FedEx becomes a parcel-focused company; LTL shippers now deal with a separate company.

headline: FedEx raises domestic fuel table pivot points (diesel $4.99, jet $3.01)
details: Ground/Home Delivery/Intl Ground diesel table pivot moved from $3.55 to $4.99/gal
Below pivot: 0.25 pt per $0.27 diesel change; at/above: per $0.09
Express jet-fuel pivot reportedly $2.06 to $3.01/gal; surcharge higher than old table below pivot
note: Step sizes confirmed on FedEx page; pivot values and effective date from one secondary source. A reported Mar 2026 +1 pt change (Loop) not confirmed.

headline: FedEx merges U.S. export and import fuel tables; exports pay more
details: Separate export and import international fuel surcharge tables consolidated into one table
Raises export fuel surcharge (reported +3.5 pts) and lowers import
note: +3.5 pt export figure from TransImpact headline only.

headline: FedEx 2026 GRI: 5.9% average; Freight 5.9-6.9%
details: Standard list rates for U.S., U.S. export and U.S. import package services: avg 5.9%
Ground Economy, Ground Multiweight, International Premium rates also rise; % not specified
FedEx Freight: avg 5.9%; 6.9% for FXF 1000, FXF 501, FXFM Mexico door-to-door and intra-Mexico
AHS, Delivery Area, Residential, Oversize, Declared Value, Ground Unauthorized charges also increase
Third straight 5.9% headline (2024, 2025, 2026)
note: Announcement date not confirmed: one source says Sept 12, 2025, another 'early October'; trade coverage mid-Sept 2025. Residential surcharge increase ~8.4% per PARCEL Industry.

headline: 2026 demand surcharges: residential up to $0.80, Ground Economy $4.05
details: AHS/oversize/unauthorized demand charges from Sept 28, 2026; residential and Express demand charges from Oct 26; program ends Jan 17, 2027
Peak window Nov 23 - Dec 27, 2026: Ground Residential/Home Delivery $0.80 (vs $0.65 in 2025), Ground Economy $4.05, Overnight $2.55
Peak window: AHS $11.85 (vs $10.90), Oversize $117.25 (vs $108.50), Ground Unauthorized $595
Sept 21, 2026: international demand surcharge adjusted; Demand-Ground Unauthorized renamed Demand-Unauthorized
note: July 22 from two secondary sources and SCD 'Wednesday'; AFMS says July 23. AHS/oversize peak amounts from vendor blogs. FedEx page also describes weekly peaking-factor residential charge for large shippers.

headline: FedEx adds cubic-volume triggers to Additional Handling and Oversize
details: AHS-Dimension now also applies to any package > 10,368 cubic inches (L x W x H)
Oversize Charge adds cubic volume > 17,280 cubic inches and a weight criterion (110 lb reported)
New criteria are layered on top of existing length/girth rules
note: Announced with the 2026 GRI. 110 lb oversize weight trigger seen on a FedEx page excerpt; verify against Service Guide.

headline: Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs; de minimis suspension stays in place
details: Learning Resources v. Trump, 6-3: IEEPA does not authorize tariffs
Administration ended IEEPA-based tariffs effective Feb 24, 2026; shifting to Sections 122, 232, 301, 338
New proclamation kept the de minimis suspension in effect; refunds handled by lower courts
why: Changed duty rates on imported goods while low-value parcels still lost de minimis treatment.
note: Replacement tariff rates and the de minimis proclamation details not verified in this pass.

headline: FAST Group (Sendle, ACI Logistix, FirstMile) winds down after failing to raise capital
details: Customer notice: wind-down effective immediately; could not secure capital
Sendle stopped accepting parcels Jan 11, 2026
Investor Federation Asset Management alleged ACI Logistix did not disclose its true financial position
why: Sudden loss of a consolidator/small-shipper carrier forced customers to re-route volume quickly.
note: Exact date of the U.S. customer notice not verified.

headline: UPS and USPS finalize renewed Ground Saver final-mile agreement
details: Preliminary understanding disclosed on UPS Q3 2025 call (Oct 2025)
Agreement finalized January 2026; handoffs resumed in following weeks
Restores PO Box delivery and coverage of Alaska/Hawaii for Ground Saver
Reported ramp to ~1.5M average daily parcels to USPS in Q2 2026
why: Reverses the 2025 insourcing, lowering UPS's cost to serve light residential parcels and restoring coverage.
note: Exact finalization date not verified; 1.5M/day figure appears only in low-quality aggregator reprints of the Q1 2026 call.

headline: UPS Mail Innovations DIM divisor reported to change 166 -> 139
details: UPS Mail Innovations domestic surcharge doc 'Effective July 12, 2026' says DIM divisor changes 166 -> 139
note: Seen only through a search summary of the UPS PDF. Appears to apply only to Mail Innovations. Not covered by trade press.

headline: UPS raises domestic fuel surcharge tables ~1 point
details: Ground domestic, Ground Saver and domestic Air tables raised, effective Jan 5, 2026
Example: Ground at $3.85 diesel 20.75% -> 21.75%
note: Single trade source.

headline: UPS raises domestic fuel tables again; third increase of 2026
details: +1 point to domestic fuel surcharge table (FreightWaves: Mar 9; third UPS fuel increase of 2026)
Example: Ground at $3.85 diesel 21.75% -> 22.75%; applies to Ground, Air, Ground Saver
note: Exact date unclear: early March per SCD, Mar 9 per FreightWaves. The second 2026 increase (between Jan and Mar) was not identified.

headline: UPS 2026 GRI: 5.9% average; residential surcharge $6.50, LPS up ~9-10%
details: Average 5.9% for Ground, Air and International, effective Dec 22, 2025 (2 weeks before FedEx)
Ground Saver average net +5.9%, effective Dec 22, 2025 (UPS Ground Saver page)
Ground Residential Surcharge $6.10 -> $6.50; Ground residential DAS $6.15 -> $6.55
LPS examples: commercial Zone 5-6 $250 -> $273; residential Zone 3-4 $260 -> $286
ZIP-to-zone alignments adjusted
note: Exact announcement date not confirmed (after FedEx's Sept 2025 announcement). A blog claim that Air took effect Jan 6, 2026 is unconfirmed and excluded.

headline: UPS plans up to 30,000 more job cuts and 24 building closures in 2026
details: Announced with Q4 2025 results; mostly via attrition and a second driver buyout
24 buildings to close in first half of 2026, more under review
Plans to cut ~25 million operational hours tied to Amazon volume
why: Continued UPS network contraction affects capacity, service footprint and pricing.

headline: UPS 2026 peak: LPS $96.25-$117.50, OML $530-$590; demand from Oct 25
details: Windows: Sep 27 - Nov 21; Nov 22 - Dec 26 (peak); Dec 27, 2026 - Jan 16, 2027
Large Package $96.25 / $117.50 / $96.25; Over Maximum Limits $530 / $590 / $530
Additional Handling reported $8.75 / $11.90 / $8.75
Ground Residential and Ground Saver demand $0.50 / $0.75 / $0.50 from Oct 25 (UPS); SCD: $0.50-$2.50 across Ground Res, Air, Ground Saver
Higher-volume tables for customers >20,000 pkgs/week after Oct 2025, vs June 2026 baseline
note: LPS/OML/windows are from the UPS 'August 26, 2026 Update'. AHS amounts are from secondary consultancy sources only. The top higher-volume tier conflicts ($8.00 UPS doc summary vs $9.35 SCD).

headline: UPS and USPS renew Ground Saver final-mile deal
details: USPS to deliver some Ground Saver and Mail Innovations parcels; handoffs began January 2026
Q1 2026: ~977,000 parcels/day to USPS, about 44% of Ground Saver volume
note: The announced date is SCD's report date. Pricing changes from the deal not confirmed.

headline: UPS moves AHS and Large Package triggers to cubic-volume thresholds
details: Large Package: cubic size >17,280 cu in or weight >110 lb, replacing length-plus-girth test
Additional Handling: cubic size >10,368 cu in
First scheduled for Aug 17, 2025, then postponed to Jan 26, 2026
note: The Aug 2025 plan reportedly used 8,640 cu in for AHS. Other existing AHS triggers (weight, length) reportedly unchanged; not verified.

headline: UPS surge fee on U.S.-Middle East shipments
details: UPS surge fee notice: $1.34/lb U.S.-Middle East, $1.50/lb U.S.-UAE, effective Mar 22, 2026 until further notice
SCD earlier reported a $0.64/lb surge fee for 15 Middle East countries
note: UPS document and SCD amounts conflict, possibly from successive revisions. The UPS doc is the Oct 15, 2026 version.

headline: New hazmat handling fee on parcels containing hazardous materials
details: Hazmat Handling Fee on all pieces containing hazardous materials: PME, Priority Mail, Ground Advantage, Parcel Select (retail and commercial)
Trade sources report a $50 hazmat noncompliance fee for Ground Advantage
note: Hazmat handling fee amount not retrieved; $50 noncompliance fee from a single trade source.

headline: DIM divisor cut from 166 to 139; package dimensions rounded up to whole inch
details: DIM divisor 166 to 139 for packages over 1 cubic foot (1,728 cu in)
Applies to retail and commercial Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, Ground Advantage, Parcel Select
Length, width and height rounded up to the next whole inch before calculation
note: Some secondary sources describe rounding of final billable weight rather than dimensions; USPS final rule describes rounding dimensions.

headline: 2026 peak surcharge Oct 4, 2026 - Jan 17, 2027, stacked on the temporary 8%
details: Ran Oct 4, 2026 to Jan 17, 2027; PME, Priority Mail, Ground Advantage, Parcel Select
Per-package increases $0.40 to $20.80 depending on tier, service, zone, weight
Retail PM & Ground Advantage Z1-4: +$0.50 (0-3 lb), +$0.80 (4-10), +$1.25 (11-25), +$3.90 (26-70 and oversized)
Commercial PM & Ground Advantage Z1-4 26-70 lb: +$3.15
Applies on top of the April 2026 8% temporary increase
note: PRC approval reported as Sept 9, 2026 by a single trade source (FP-USA); not checked against PRC order. Zones 5-9 amounts not retrieved. A '6%' headline figure from one blog is unverified.

headline: January 2026 price change: PM +6.6%, PME +5.1%, Ground Advantage +7.8%, Parcel Select +6%
details: Priority Mail: ~+6.6%
Priority Mail Express: ~+5.1%
USPS Ground Advantage: ~+7.8%
Parcel Select: ~+6.0%
Results vary by weight/zone; some commercial cells decreased (trade reports)
note: PRC approval reported late December 2025 by trade sources; order number not retrieved.

headline: Temporary 8% transportation-related increase on parcel base postage, through Jan 17, 2027
details: +8% on base postage for Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, Ground Advantage and Parcel Select
In effect Apr 26, 2026 to Jan 17, 2027 (midnight CT)
Governors approved Mar 24, 2026; filed with PRC Mar 25
Stated purpose: align prices with transportation costs; no other products affected
note: Unscheduled mid-year shipping increase. PRC docket not confirmed (one summary cites CP2026-10 / Order 9703, another assigns CP2026-10 to the holiday filing).

headline: July 2026 change: Ground Advantage Commercial ounce tiers removed (+11.8% avg)
details: Ounce-based rate differentiation for Ground Advantage Commercial eliminated: avg +11.8% for GA Commercial
Ground Advantage retail prices unchanged
Ground Advantage Cubic soft pack tiers reduced from 10 to 5; package intercept pricing revised
Competitive PO Box prices +3%
Docket CP2026-8 (Shipping Services)
note: pct applies to Ground Advantage Commercial only. Priority Mail change not confirmed from USPS (Stamps.com cites ~6.6%, which matches the January figure and may be a mislabel; ship.com says base rates unchanged). Negotiated-rate customers reportedly unaffected by the ounce-tier change.

headline: Amazon taps FedEx for large-package residential deliveries, first deal since 2019
details: Multi-year agreement reportedly signed February 2025, disclosed May 2025
FedEx delivers select large/heavy Amazon packages
Amazon called FedEx one of several partners alongside UPS and USPS
why: Signaled Amazon backfilling UPS volume and FedEx competing for bulky residential freight.
note: Exact disclosure day in May 2025 not verified.

headline: FedEx rounds every fractional inch up for dimensional weight
details: Any fraction of an inch/cm rounded up to the next whole unit (previously < 0.5 rounded down)
Raises DIM weight on many parcels; can push more packages over AHS and unauthorized thresholds
UPS adopted the same rule on the same date
note: Announcement date not confirmed.

headline: FedEx updates domestic and international fuel surcharge tables
details: FedEx published domestic fuel tables effective June 9, 2025 (Ground, International Ground, Freight) and updated Express tables
note: Magnitude of shift not captured here.

headline: FedEx raises domestic fuel indexes; Ground ~+1.5 pts
details: Domestic Ground fuel surcharge 20.75% to 22.25% at constant fuel prices
Domestic Air 20.00% to 21.75%
UPS made a similar change at the same time
note: Announcement date not confirmed.

headline: FedEx 2025 GRI: 5.9% average on Express, Ground, Home Delivery, Freight
details: Avg 5.9% across Express, Ground, Home Delivery and Freight (incl. Freight Priority/Economy)
Additional Handling up ~25.9%-28.2% and Oversize up ~26.1%-28.6% depending on service/zone (Reveel)
AHS-Dimension 2025: $28 (Zone 2) to $38 (Zone 7+); Oversize: $205 (Zone 2) to $260 (Zone 7+) (Sifted)
Ground/Home Delivery DAS up ~8.8%; Extended DAS up ~7.1%-7.8%
note: Announcement date from AFMS plus Supply Chain Dive ('Friday', article Sept 16, 2024). Surcharge % from consultancies.

headline: 2025 demand surcharges: residential up to $0.65, Ground Economy up to $3.55
details: AHS/oversize/unauthorized demand charges Sept 29, 2025 - Jan 18, 2026; Demand AHS $8.25 to $10.90
Ground residential and Home Delivery: $0.40 (Oct 27 - Nov 23), $0.65 (Nov 24 - Dec 28), $0.40 (Dec 29 - Jan 18, 2026)
Ground Economy: $2.20 / $3.55 / $2.20 over the same windows
Enterprise Demand Residential Delivery Charge (>20,000 pkgs/week): $1.55 to $8.75 per package by peaking factor vs June 2025 baseline
note: July 8, 2025 from Lojistic; Supply Chain Dive says 'Tuesday' (consistent). Oversize range ($90-$108.50) from a vendor only. Some sources give a conflicting Oct 7 - Jan 19 window.

headline: U.S. ends duty-free de minimis entry for goods from China and Hong Kong
details: Order announced April 2, 2025; effective May 2, 2025 for goods ≤$800
Postal items: 30% duty or $25/item, rising to $50/item after June 1, 2025
Aimed at low-value Chinese e-commerce shipments
why: Raised landed cost of direct-from-China e-commerce, cutting cross-border parcel volume into U.S. networks.
note: Postal duty rates were changed several times during 2025; figures shown are from the April 2025 order.

headline: One Big Beautiful Bill Act repeals statutory de minimis for commercial shipments from July 2027
details: H.R. 1 signed July 4, 2025; Section 70531
Repeal effective July 1, 2027
Adds civil penalties for de minimis misuse ($5,000 first, $10,000 repeat)
why: Makes the end of de minimis permanent in law, not only by executive order.
note: Sources disagree whether the repeal is total or limited to commercial shipments; statute text not reviewed directly.

headline: U.S. suspends de minimis duty-free treatment for imports from all countries
details: Executive Order 14324 signed July 30, 2025; effective 12:01 a.m. ET Aug 29, 2025
Applies regardless of value, origin or mode
Postal shipments pay IEEPA duty rate or a per-package fee; some foreign posts paused U.S. shipments
why: Every low-value import now needs duty and entry handling, raising cross-border parcel costs and complexity.
note: Claim that foreign posts paused shipments is widely reported but not verified in this pass.

headline: Amazon becomes largest U.S. parcel carrier by volume in 2025
details: Pitney Bowes 2026 index: 23.1B U.S. parcels in 2025 (+3.3%); Amazon 6.9B, largest carrier
ShipMatrix: Amazon 6.7B vs USPS 6.6B; UPS 4.4B (-8.6%); FedEx 3.6B
UPS revenue share fell to 31.6% (Pitney Bowes); revenue grew faster than volume
why: Amazon's own network now out-delivers every incumbent, reducing its dependence on UPS/USPS and reshaping carrier economics.
note: Pitney Bowes and ShipMatrix differ on Amazon's 2025 volume (6.9B vs 6.7B). Pitney Bowes 2025 USPS figure not retrieved.

headline: Sendle, ACI Logistix and FirstMile merge to form FAST Group
details: ACI Logistix-led scrip merger with Sendle and FirstMile, August 2025
Aimed to be a North American parcel distribution platform for all shipper sizes
why: Consolidated several consolidator/small-shipper options under one company.
note: Exact merger close date not verified.

headline: Alternative carriers such as UniUni and GOFO surge on Temu/Shein volume
details: Pitney Bowes: 'Other' carriers' revenue share rose from 3.4% (2024) to 7.2% (2025); volume reportedly +127%
UniUni says domestic volume rose 1,073% in 2025 and coverage reached 65% of U.S. population
GOFO reported >2.5M parcels in a single day in Dec 2025; over half its volume reportedly from Temu and Shein
why: Added low-cost residential delivery capacity outside UPS/FedEx/USPS, widening shipper options.
note: Carrier figures are self-reported or from regional trade press; the 127% base is unclear. Better Trucks growth could not be verified (conflicting funding data) and is omitted.

headline: UPS updates Delivery Area Surcharge ZIP code list
details: List of ZIP codes subject to Delivery Area Surcharge changed effective June 1, 2025
note: Single trade source. ZIPs added or removed not reported.

headline: UPS agrees with Amazon to cut Amazon volume by more than 50%
details: Announced with Q4 2024 results on Jan 30, 2025
Agreement in principle to lower Amazon volume by >50% by the second half of 2026
CEO Carol Tomé: Amazon is largest but not most profitable customer; volume 'very dilutive'
UPS shares fell ~14% that day
why: Triggered UPS network shrinkage and building closures and freed Amazon to grow its own network.
note: Some outlets say 'by June 2026'; UPS wording referenced the second half of 2026.

headline: UPS completes ~US$1.6B acquisition of Andlauer Healthcare Group
details: Announced April 2025; C$55.00/share, ~C$2.2B (US$1.6B)
Follows UPS's 2025 acquisition of Germany's Frigo-Trans (cold-chain)
Michael Andlauer leads UPS Canada Healthcare and AHG
why: Deepened UPS's shift to healthcare logistics as it shed low-margin Amazon volume.
note: Frigo-Trans/BPL acquisition not separately verified (one passing mention only); no date given.

headline: UPS raises domestic Ground, SurePost, Air fuel tables 50 bp
details: +0.50 points on fuel surcharge tables for U.S. Ground, SurePost and domestic Air, effective Mar 10, 2025

headline: UPS raises domestic fuel surcharge tables 100 bp
details: +1.00 point on domestic Ground, Air and Ground Saver fuel tables, effective May 26, 2025
Example: at $3.20 diesel, Ground 17.75% -> 18.75%
note: Single trade source.

headline: UPS 2025 GRI: 5.9% average net; new AHS 40 lb minimum billable weight
details: Average 5.9% for Ground, Air and International, effective Dec 23, 2024 (2 weeks before FedEx)
UPS 10-Q: 5.9% average net increase in base and accessorial rates, Air and Ground
Minimum billable weight of 40 lb for packages that get Additional Handling on dimensions
PARCEL est. AHS and LPS up 26.5%+ on average; DAS ZIP list changed
note: Exact announcement date not confirmed. SCD reported it on Oct 9, 2024.

headline: UPS plans ~20,000 job cuts and 73 building closures tied to Amazon glide-down
details: Announced with Q1 2025 results
Expected ~$3.5B savings in 2025 from Network Reconfiguration and Efficiency Reimagined
By Q3 2025 UPS reported ~34,000 operational positions cut and 93 buildings closed in the first nine months
why: Shrank UPS ground capacity and density, changing service coverage and rate strategy.
note: Some outlets report 48,000 total jobs cut in 2025 (including management); counts differ by scope.

headline: UPS 2025 peak: AHS $8.25-$10.80, LPS $90.50-$107, OML $485-$540
details: Sep 28, 2025 - Jan 17, 2026; highest rates Nov 23 - Dec 27, 2025
Additional Handling $8.25 / $10.80; Large Package $90.50 / $107; Over Maximum Limits $485 / $540
Demand surcharge Ground Residential, Air, Ground Saver $0.40-$2.05 per package, Oct 26, 2025 - Jan 17, 2026
Higher-volume tier up to $8.75 for customers >20,000 pkgs/week after Oct 2024, vs June 2025 baseline
note: Figures are from the UPS 'August 28, 2025 Update'. Original announcement date not confirmed.

headline: UPS SurePost rate increase effective Jan 13, 2025
details: Separate SurePost rate change effective Jan 13, 2025, after the end of the USPS SurePost partnership
note: Single trade source. Size of the increase not confirmed.

headline: UPS renames SurePost as UPS Ground Saver
details: SurePost renamed Ground Saver after the USPS final-mile partnership ended at end of 2024
No formal announcement; UPS Ground Saver terms are dated effective Mar 31, 2025
note: Effective date is from the terms document. No official date for the rename itself.

headline: UPS fully insources SurePost, ending USPS final-mile handoff; product becomes Ground Saver
details: UPS said 100% of SurePost was insourced as of Jan 1, 2025 (disclosed Jan 30, 2025)
Cited USPS service deterioration and planned USPS price increases
UPS cited a 9.9% average SurePost rate increase
Product later renamed UPS Ground Saver (reported April 2025)
why: Raised costs for economy residential parcels and removed PO Box/USPS-delivered option until 2026.
note: Insourcing effective 2025-01-01 is confirmed (not 2024 as sometimes stated, though UPS began shifting volume during 2024). The Ground Saver rename date (April 2, 2025) comes only from secondary blogs and is unconfirmed; the 9.9% figure is from a call-transcript summary.

headline: UPS swaps 2% card surcharge for 2% payment processing fee; new billing fees
details: 2% payment processing fee per invoice replaces 2% credit card surcharge
$5 per printed invoice copy; $25 per check or wire payment
Late payment fee 8% -> 9.9% of past-due balance
note: Effective date conflicts: May 18 (SCD) vs May 19 (PARCEL). Effective dates of the other fees not confirmed.

headline: DFA service standard changes incl. Regional Transportation Optimization (RTO)
details: Mail from ZIP Codes >50 miles from the regional processing center collected next day rather than same day (RTO)
Most packages keep same standard; some get one extra day (USPS)
Sundays/holidays no longer counted for mail entered Saturday or day before a holiday
USPS projected ~$3B annual savings
note: Federal Register rule chiefly covers market-dominant standards (39 CFR 121; part effective July 1, 2025). Exact package (Ground Advantage/Priority) standard changes and share of volume slowed not quantified from a primary source. Proposed rule published Feb 28, 2025 (FR 2025-03168).

headline: Postmaster General Louis DeJoy steps down; David Steiner named successor
details: DeJoy's resignation effective March 24, 2025; Deputy PMG Doug Tulino served as acting PMG
Board of Governors named David Steiner (ex-Waste Management CEO, FedEx board member) 76th PMG on May 9, 2025
Steiner took office in July 2025
why: New leadership reopened USPS's posture toward workshare and last-mile partnerships with private carriers.
note: Exact day Steiner took office in July 2025 not verified.

headline: USPS reports $9.0B net loss for fiscal 2025
details: FY2025 (ended Sept 30, 2025) net loss $9.0B vs $9.5B in FY2024
Operating revenue $80.5B, +1.2%, led by Ground Advantage and price increases
Controllable loss widened to $2.7B from $1.8B on weak package revenue
why: Ongoing losses drive USPS price increases and openness to new private-carrier deals.
note: Earlier years' losses (FY2021-FY2024) not individually verified except FY2024 ($9.5B).

headline: 2025 peak surcharge on PM, PME, Ground Advantage and Parcel Select, Oct 5, 2025 - Jan 18, 2026
details: Ran Oct 5, 2025 to Jan 18, 2026 (Governors approved Aug 7)
Products: Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, Ground Advantage, Parcel Select
Priority Mail & Ground Advantage Z1-4 0-3 lb: +$0.40
Priority Mail Z5-9 0-3 lb: +$0.90
Priority Mail Z5-9 26-70 lb: +$7.00 (per reprints of USPS release)
note: Full table not retrieved; whether the cited amounts are commercial or retail not confirmed. Walsworth shows $6.50 for PM Z5-9 26-70 lb (possibly the other price tier).

headline: January 2025 price change: PM/PME +3.2%, Ground Advantage +3.9%, Parcel Select +9.2%
details: Priority Mail: +3.2%
Priority Mail Express: +3.2%
USPS Ground Advantage: +3.9%
Parcel Select: +9.2%
No January increase for Mailing Services (stamps unchanged)

headline: Mid-year July 2025 change: Priority Mail +6.3%, Ground Advantage +7.1%, Parcel Select +7.6%
details: Priority Mail: ~+6.3%
USPS Ground Advantage: ~+7.1% overall; retail +9.8%, commercial +4.7% (Federal Register)
Parcel Select: ~+7.6%
Priority Mail Express: no change
Ground Advantage Commercial packages become sealed against inspection
note: Priority Mail commercial/retail split (5.1% / 7.3%) appears in only one trade article; not used as confirmed. PRC approval date not retrieved.

headline: FedEx's USPS air transportation contract expires after talks fail
details: FedEx disclosed in an SEC filing that talks ended March 29, 2024
Contract expired Sept 29, 2024
FedEx booked ~$1.7B from USPS in FY2023, down from ~$2.4B in FY2020
why: Removed a major base load from FedEx's Express air network, accelerating its air network downsizing.

headline: FedEx announces plan to spin off FedEx Freight as a separate public company
details: Board approved full separation; targeted within ~18 months
Tax-free spin-off of the largest North American LTL carrier
why: Refocused FedEx on parcel; set up separate pricing and relationships for LTL customers.

headline: FedEx international fuel surcharge table update
details: FedEx lists an international fuel table update effective Oct 7, 2024
note: Confirmed only for international tables via a non-U.S. FedEx page; U.S. domestic impact and magnitude unknown.

headline: FedEx 2024 GRI: 5.9% Express/Ground/Home Delivery; Freight 5.9-6.9%
details: Express U.S. domestic/export/import: avg 5.9%; Ground and Home Delivery: avg 5.9%
FedEx Freight: avg 5.9%-6.9% by rate scale
Ground Economy rates increased; % not stated
AHS-Dimension Zone 2: $18.50 to $22; AHS-Weight Zone 7+: $36 to $43.50 (FedEx surcharge sheet)
Residential DAS: $5.55 to $5.85; Oversize Zone 2: $135 to $160 (Sifted)
Jan 15, 2024: AHS and Oversize assessed per package (not per shipment) on international multi-piece shipments
note: Full rate details posted on fedex.com Sept 7, 2023.

headline: 2024 demand surcharges: AHS up to $10, new $0.30-$0.55 Ground residential fee
details: AHS/oversize/unauthorized demand charges from Sept 30, 2024; residential demand from Oct 28; program ends Jan 19, 2025
Demand AHS: $7.75 (Sept 30 - Nov 24), $10.00 (Nov 25 - Dec 29), $7.75 (from Dec 30)
Ground residential demand surcharge: $0.30 to $0.55 per package
Enterprise Residential Delivery Charge (>20,000 residential + Ground Economy pkgs/week): $1.45 to $8.25 per package
note: Announced Aug 2024; exact date not confirmed. Oversize tiers reported by one vendor ($84.50/$100) not confirmed. Ground Economy amounts not captured.

headline: Pitney Bowes exits Global Ecommerce; GEC entities file Chapter 11 for liquidation
details: Controlling interest sold to a Hilco Global affiliate on Aug 8, 2024
Two GEC entities filed Chapter 11; ~$45M DIP financing from a PB subsidiary
GEC lost ~$136M in 2023; wind-down expected to finish early 2025
Fulfillment business sold separately to Stord
why: Removed a large parcel consolidator, pushing its shippers to other carriers and consolidators.

headline: U.S. parcel volume rises 3.4% to 22.4 billion; Amazon closes in on USPS
details: Pitney Bowes: 22.4B parcels in 2024; revenue +2.7% to $203.2B
USPS 6.9B; Amazon 6.3B (+7.3%); FedEx fell to 3.7B from 3.9B
Revenue share: UPS 34%, FedEx 31%, USPS 16%, Amazon 15.3%
'Other' carriers grew 23% to 0.8B parcels
why: Growth returned modestly while share kept moving to Amazon and alternative carriers.
note: Pitney Bowes release dated June 2025. UPS 2024 volume not captured in retrieved summaries.

headline: UPS becomes USPS's primary domestic air cargo provider, replacing FedEx
details: UPS announced April 1, 2024; contract runs at least 5.5 years per USPS
Covers most USPS domestic air for First-Class, Priority Mail and Priority Mail Express
Terms not disclosed
why: Shifted a large air base load from FedEx to UPS, affecting both carriers' air network economics.

headline: UPS raises domestic Ground, Air, SurePost fuel tables 50 bp
details: Domestic Ground, Air and SurePost fuel surcharge tables +0.50 points, effective Apr 29, 2024
Example: diesel $3.26-$3.38 band moved 14.25% -> 14.75%
note: Single trade source. SCD also reported earlier (Dec) and later (Sept 2024) fuel adjustments, but they were not researched.

headline: UPS 2024 GRI: 5.9% average net; area surcharge ZIP list changes
details: Average net 5.9% for Ground, Air and International, effective Dec 26, 2023; rates published Oct 12, 2023
UPS 10-K: 5.9% average net increase in base and accessorial rates, Air and Ground
ZIP codes subject to area surcharges and some ZIP-to-zone alignments changed
2024 DAS $3.95-$7.70; Remote Area $14.15 (excl. Alaska)
Consultant estimate: AHS and LPS up 19.5% on average
note: Announcement date of Sep 7, 2023 is from PARCEL. DAS/RAS figures are from a single search summary.

headline: UPS 2024 peak: AHS $7.75-$9.95, LPS $84.75-$99, OML $445-$495
details: Sep 29, 2024 - Jan 18, 2025; highest rates Nov 24 - Dec 28
Additional Handling $7.75 / $9.95 peak; Large Package $84.75 / $99.00 peak; Over Maximum Limits $445 / $495 peak
Residential demand (Air, Ground Residential, SurePost) from Oct 27: $0.25, $0.50 Nov 24 - Dec 28
Higher-volume tier $1.50-$8.25 per package for customers >20,000 pkgs in any week after Oct 2023
note: From the UPS Sept 16, 2024 update, read through a search summary. The $0.25/$0.50 base residential tier is not cross-checked. Original announcement date not confirmed.

headline: USPS pauses new regional processing center consolidations after service failures
details: DeJoy letter of May 9, 2024 paused further implementation until at least Jan 1, 2025
Triggered by delays at new Atlanta (Palmetto) and Richmond RPDCs; Atlanta inbound on-time rate ~36% in February 2024
Regional center build-out itself continued; decisions made for ~60 sites
why: Showed service risk in USPS's network overhaul, affecting USPS reliability for parcel shippers.
note: Status of RPDC moves after Jan 2025 not verified.

headline: 2024 peak surcharge on PM, PME and Ground Advantage, Oct 6, 2024 - Jan 19, 2025
details: Ran Oct 6, 2024 to Jan 19, 2025 (Governors approved Aug 8)
Products: Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, Ground Advantage; commercial and retail; Parcel Select not listed
Priority Mail Z5-9 0-3 lb: +$0.70
note: Amount table only partly retrieved; commercial vs retail labeling of the Z1-4 figures not verified. Walsworth gives end date Jan 18, 2025 vs USPS Jan 19. PRC approval not separately confirmed.

headline: January 2024 price change: Ground Advantage +5.4%, Priority Mail +5.7%, Express +5.9%
details: USPS Ground Advantage: +5.4%
Priority Mail: +5.7%; retail +5.6%, commercial +5.8% (Postal Bulletin)
Priority Mail Express: +5.9%
Some Ground Advantage prices decreased depending on rate card (Supply Chain Dive)
note: Any nonstandard-fee changes in January 2024 not verified.

headline: Mid-year July 2024 change: Parcel Select +25% average; other parcels unchanged
details: Parcel Select: +25% average
No increase for Ground Advantage, Priority Mail or Priority Mail Express
note: pct applies to Parcel Select only. Docket reported as CP2024-295 in a search summary; PRC approval order not retrieved.

headline: Amazon relaunches Amazon Shipping ground service to outside sellers
details: 2-5 business-day ground delivery for orders from Amazon and other channels
Packages up to 50 lb; USPS used where Amazon lacks coverage
Initially offered to a limited set of partners, then expanded
why: Added a new low-cost ground option for multichannel sellers, pressuring UPS/FedEx pricing.
note: Sources conflict on when the prior pause began (2020 vs 2022); Amazon also had other service changes in between.

headline: FedEx adjusts fuel surcharges effective March 6, 2023
details: FedEx rate-changes page lists fuel surcharge adjustment effective Mar 6, 2023, citing rising fuel and transport costs
Separately, for week of Nov 13, 2023 FedEx reused the prior week's percentage while moving to a one-week lag
note: Primary source is FedEx Mexico page; U.S. applicability and magnitude not confirmed.

headline: FedEx 2023 GRI: 6.9% Express/Ground/Home Delivery; Freight 6.9-7.9%
details: Express, Ground, Home Delivery: avg 6.9%
FedEx Freight: avg 6.9%-7.9% depending on rate scale
Announced with Q1 FY23 results; FedEx cited 'the inflationary backdrop'
Largest headline GRI in FedEx history per FreightWaves
note: Structural surcharge changes for 2023 not captured in this pass.

headline: FedEx plans 'one FedEx' consolidation and Network 2.0 merging Express and Ground
details: Announced April 2023: Express, Ground and Services to merge into Federal Express Corporation effective June 2024
Network 2.0 combines U.S./Canada Express and Ground pickup and delivery ('one truck, one label')
FedEx Freight kept separate
why: Changes pickup/delivery operations and service footprint for FedEx shippers; aims at large cost savings.
note: Exact announcement day in April 2023 not verified. Network 2.0 savings targets vary by source ($2B by FY27 for Network 2.0 alone vs $6B combined with DRIVE).

headline: 2023 demand surcharges: AHS $6.95, oversize $73, 'peak' renamed 'demand'
details: Peak surcharges rebranded 'Demand' surcharges effective Sept 4, 2023
Demand AHS: $6.95/pkg, Oct 2, 2023 - Jan 14, 2024
Demand Oversize: $73/pkg; Ground Unauthorized: $410/pkg (Oct 2 - Jan 14)
Ground Economy: $1.60 (Oct 30 - Nov 26), $2.60 (Nov 27 - Dec 10), $1.60 (Dec 11 - Jan 14, 2024)
Residential Delivery Charge for enterprise shippers set weekly by peaking factor
note: Aug 29, 2023 is the date of FedEx's update notice (same day as 2024 GRI release). Residential tier range (one snippet: $1.35-$6.35) truncated, not confirmed.

headline: FedEx details DRIVE, a $4B structural cost-reduction program
details: DRIVE introduced in fiscal 2023; detailed at an April 5, 2023 investor event at the NYSE
Target $4B structural cost cuts by FY2025 vs FY2023 base
FedEx reported $1.8B in FY24 and $2.2B in FY25, reaching $4.0B
Planned further ~$1B permanent cuts in FY2026 from DRIVE and Network 2.0
why: Cost focus over volume chase shaped FedEx pricing discipline and network cuts.
note: DRIVE was first referenced in late 2022 (FY23); exact first-announcement date not verified, so the April 2023 investor event date is used.

headline: Amazon Logistics passes UPS in U.S. parcel volume as market flattens
details: Pitney Bowes: 21.7B parcels in 2023 (+0.5%); revenue slipped 0.03% to $197.9B, first decline in 7 years
UPS kept largest revenue share at 35%
why: Flat demand plus Amazon's growth shifted share away from UPS/FedEx and strengthened shipper negotiating leverage.
note: Pitney Bowes says 2023 was first time Amazon passed UPS in its index; SupplyChainBrain (citing other data) says Amazon passed UPS in 2022. Methodologies differ.

headline: UPS completes acquisition of MNX Global Logistics (time-critical healthcare)
details: Announced Sept 2023; closed Nov 2, 2023 per trade press
UPS FY2023 10-K lists MNX and Happy Returns as November 2023 acquisitions
Price not disclosed
why: Part of UPS's pivot toward higher-margin healthcare logistics.
note: Close was November 2023, not January 2024.

headline: UPS 2023 GRI: 6.9% average, matching FedEx
details: Average 6.9% for Ground, Air and International, effective Dec 27, 2022
UPS Air Freight (U.S./Canada/Puerto Rico) +6.2%
Accessorials (residential, additional handling, area surcharges) also raised Dec 27
PARCEL later estimated the average UPS customer paid 10.2% more in 2023
note: Announced 'late Friday' per FreightWaves article dated Oct 23, 2022.

headline: UPS Teamsters ratify five-year contract averting strike
details: Tentative agreement reached July 25, 2023
Ratified with 86.3% approval, announced Aug 22, 2023; covers ~340,000 workers
$7.50/hr in raises over the contract ($2.75 in 2023); part-time start $21/hr
Top-rate drivers to average ~$49/hr by end of contract; Teamsters cite ~$30B in new money
7,500 new full-time jobs; A/C in new package cars from 2024
why: Raised UPS's labor cost base, feeding rate increases and diverting volume to rivals during strike fears.
note: Contract runs through July 31, 2028 (term end date not separately verified in this search).

headline: UPS extends year-round 'demand surcharges' at $0.40-$0.60 per package
details: 'Peak' surcharges renamed 'demand' surcharges, in effect Jan 15, 2023 until further notice
$0.40-$0.60 per residential package for shippers >20,000 residential pkgs/week, based on June/Sept 2022 volume
Additional Handling back to $3.50, Large Package to $40, Over Maximum Limits peak fee to $0 from Jan 15
note: The announced date is the FreightWaves article date. UPS's exact notice date was not confirmed.

headline: UPS 2023 peak: LPS $74.90; residential demand $1.35-$7.50 for large shippers
details: Large Package demand surcharge $40 -> $74.90, Oct 1, 2023 - Jan 13, 2024
Residential demand surcharge $1.35-$7.50 (Ground Residential, Air Residential, SurePost), Oct 29, 2023 - Jan 13, 2024
Applied to customers >20,000 pkgs in any week after Oct 2022
note: 2023 Additional Handling and Over Maximum peak amounts not confirmed; sources conflict. Announcement date not confirmed; SCD covered the peak fees together with the 2024 GRI.

headline: No peak/holiday surcharge for the 2023 season
details: USPS said it would not apply any peak or demand surcharge for the 2023 holidays
Ended a practice that began in 2020
USPS also cited no residential, Saturday-delivery or minimum-volume fees
note: pct 0 = no surcharge. Exact USPS announcement date not captured (reported early autumn 2023).

headline: January 2023 price change: Priority Mail ~5.5%, Express 6.6%, FCPS 7.8%
details: Priority Mail: ~+5.5% overall; commercial +3.6%
Priority Mail Express: +6.6%
First-Class Package Service: +7.8%
Parcel Select Ground: no increase (tied to service-standard improvement)

headline: USPS Ground Advantage launches, replacing FCPS, Parcel Select Ground and Retail Ground
details: First-Class Package Service rebranded as USPS Ground Advantage; Parcel Select Ground and Retail Ground folded in
Federal Register: Ground Advantage prices -1.4% overall vs predecessor products
2-5 business day delivery; up to 70 lb
Parcel Select (destination entry) remains separate product
note: Announcement date taken from USPS newsroom release URL (May 10, 2023). One trade source cites commercial rates 0.7% below predecessors; the -1.4% figure is from the Federal Register. Whether Priority Mail prices changed in July 2023 was not verified.

headline: USPS launches Ground Advantage, consolidating its ground parcel products
details: 2-5 day ground service for packages up to 70 lb
Replaced First-Class Package Service, Parcel Select Ground and Retail Ground
Parcel Select Destination Entry and Lightweight continued
why: Gave shippers a single, lower-priced USPS ground option competing directly with UPS/FedEx economy services.
note: Service launched July 9, 2023; USPS press release dated July 10, 2023.

headline: FedEx shifts fuel table trigger points, ~+1.75 pts on Express and Ground
details: New table released Mar 17, 2022, adds ~1.75 percentage points to domestic Express and Ground fuel surcharges
Fuel % also applies to accessorials (residential, DAS, AHS, oversize, signature)
note: Single secondary source (AFS); year inferred from article context. Needs FedEx primary confirmation.

headline: FedEx 2022 GRI: 5.9% Express/Ground/Home Delivery; Freight 5.9-7.9%
details: Express U.S. domestic/export/import: avg 5.9%
Ground and Home Delivery: avg 5.9%
FedEx Freight: 5.9% (FXF PZONE/EZONE), 7.9% (FXF 1000/501)
First break from the ~4.9% annual pattern
New freight and delivery surcharges effective Jan 17, 2022

headline: 2022 peak: AHS $6.55, oversize $68.75, tiered residential $1.25-$6.00
details: Peak AHS: $6.55/pkg from Oct 3, 2022 (from $3.45 non-holiday demand level)
Peak Oversize: $68.75/pkg from Oct 3 (from $39.50)
Ground Unauthorized: $385/pkg, Oct 3, 2022 - Jan 15, 2023
Ground Economy: $1.50 (Oct 31 - Nov 27), $2.50 (Nov 28 - Dec 11), $1.50 (Dec 12 - Jan 15, 2023)
Residential Delivery Charge from Oct 31 for enterprise shippers >20,000 residential + Ground Economy pkgs/week; Ground tiers $1.25-$6.00 by peaking factor vs June 6 - July 3 baseline
note: Announcement date not confirmed (approx. Aug 2022).

headline: Veho raises $170M at $1.5B valuation weeks after reaching unicorn status
details: Dec 2021: $125M round led by Construct Capital at $1B valuation; 14 U.S. cities, target 50 markets by end-2022
Feb 2022: $170M Series B led by Tiger Global, SoftBank Vision Fund 2 participating
Next-day e-commerce delivery using crowdsourced drivers
why: Signaled heavy investor backing for venture-funded alternatives to UPS/FedEx residential delivery.
note: Veho's later scale/market count not verified.

headline: UPS raises domestic air and ground fuel surcharge tables
details: Fuel surcharge tables raised for domestic air and ground, including transborder, effective Jan 3, 2022
TransImpact estimated surcharge levels up 8%-10%; third UPS fuel hike in under 8 months
note: Both sources are FreightWaves. Exact table changes not confirmed.

headline: UPS 2022 GRI: 5.9% average net; residential surcharge to $4.85
details: Average net 5.9% for Ground, Air and International, effective Dec 26, 2021
UPS Air Freight (U.S./Canada/Puerto Rico) +5.2% average net
Ground Residential Surcharge $4.45 -> $4.85 (UPS accessorial preview)
Large Package +8%-16.7% and Additional Handling +5.2%-13.9% depending on zone
note: Announced late October 2021 (Logistics Management, Nov 1, 2021: 'late last week'). Exact date not confirmed.

headline: UPS 2022 peak: AHS $6.50, LPS $70, OML $400; residential $1.25-$7
details: Oct 2, 2022 - Jan 14, 2023: Additional Handling $3.50 -> $6.50; Large Package $40 -> $70; Over Maximum Limits $400
Residential Oct 30, 2022 - Jan 14, 2023 for shippers >20,000 pkgs/week after Oct 2021
Ground Residential and SurePost $1.25-$6.00; Air Residential $2.25-$7.00
note: Announced late August 2022. Exact date not confirmed.

headline: Nonstandard fees introduced for long and large parcels
details: Applies to PME, Priority Mail, FCPS-Retail, Retail Ground and Parcel Select pieces exceeding sortation dimensions; not Flat Rate, Regional Rate or returns
Tiers: length >22 in up to 30 in; length >30 in; volume >2 cubic feet
Dimension-noncompliance fee for commercial manifests missing accurate dimensions on pieces >22 in
USPS notified PRC on Dec 3, 2021 that implementation was delayed from Jan 2022 to April 3, 2022
Initial amounts (trade sources): $4 for 22-30 in; $15 for >30 in; $15 for >2 cu ft
Oct 2026 amounts (Pirate Ship / USPS): Ground Advantage $4.50 / $10 / $21; Priority Mail $4.50 / $21 / $35
note: Existence, tiers and April 3, 2022 date are primary-sourced. Dollar amounts by year come from trade sources; fees were revised in January 2023 and later (a 2023-era list shows $4 / $15 PM, $7 ground / $25 PM, $15 ground) but exact dates of each revision not verified. 'announced' is the Federal Register publication date.

headline: Slower service standards for ~32% of First-Class Package Service volume (DFA)
details: 32% of FCPS volume: service standard lengthened by 1-2 days
4% upgraded from 3-day to 2-day; 64% unaffected
Goal: move more long-distance volume by surface instead of air (Delivering for America)
PRC advisory opinion (Docket N2021-2) said the change would not substantially affect USPS finances
Originally planned for Oct 1, 2021, postponed
note: The Oct 1, 2021 DFA service-standard change applied to First-Class Mail and Periodicals (letter mail), not packages. PRC estimated 31.2% of FCPS volume slowed in its 2021 review.

headline: 2022 peak surcharge, Oct 2, 2022 - Jan 22, 2023
details: Ran Oct 2, 2022 to Jan 22, 2023; PRC approved Sept 6, 2022
Products: Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, FCPS, Parcel Select, USPS Retail Ground (commercial and retail)
Commercial Priority Mail: +$0.25 Z1-4 0-10 lb ... +$3.00 Z1-4 26-70 lb
Commercial FCPS / Parcel Select Ground / Retail Ground: Z1-4 +$0.25 (0-10 lb), +$0.75 (11-25), +$3.00 (26-70); Z5-9 +$0.40, +$1.60, +$5.50
Retail Priority Mail: +$0.30 Z1-4 0-10 lb; +$3.25 Z1-4 26-70 lb
note: Zones 5-9 26-70 lb retail figure conflicts across secondary sources ($6.45 vs $6.50); omitted. Ground-product table from Stamps.com summary.

headline: January 2022 price change: Priority Mail and Express +3.1%; ground products cut
details: Priority Mail: ~+3.1% (USPS)
Priority Mail Express: +3.1% overall; retail +2.9%, commercial +4.3% (Federal Register)
First-Class Package Service: +8.8% overall (Federal Register)
Parcel Select Destination Entry: -11.1% average (Federal Register)
USPS Retail Ground: -7.4% average (Federal Register)
Same filing created nonstandard fees (implementation delayed to April 3, 2022)
note: PRC docket reported as CP2022-22 (from Federal Register notice summary). Trade figures differ (Easyship: Priority Mail +2.7%, FCPS +7.4%; Stamps.com: Parcel Select Ground -12.1%). Effective date Jan 9, 2022 per DMM archive and trade sources.

headline: FedEx increases fuel surcharge tables for Express, Ground and Freight
details: Tables raised for domestic package/air, Ground, Home Delivery, International Ground; also FedEx Freight
Lower price-per-gallon rows widened
Announced with 2022 GRI release (Sept 20, 2021)
note: Magnitude of the table shift (percentage points) not captured.

headline: FedEx 2021 GRI: 4.9% Express/Ground/Home Delivery; Freight 4.9-5.9%; 6% late fee
details: Express U.S. domestic/export/import: avg 4.9%
Ground and Home Delivery: avg 4.9%
FedEx Freight: 4.9% (FXF PZONE/EZONE), 5.9% (FXF 1000/501)
New 6% late fee for Express/Ground customers not paying on agreed terms
Surcharge changes effective Jan 18, 2021, incl. revised Additional Handling Surcharge

headline: 2021 peak: AHS $5.95, oversize $62.50, Ground Economy up to $3
details: Peak AHS (U.S. Express, U.S. Ground, Intl Ground): $5.95/pkg, Oct 4, 2021 - Jan 16, 2022
Peak Oversize: $62.50/pkg, Oct 4, 2021 - Jan 16, 2022
Residential charge for high-volume shippers; threshold lowered to 25,000 pkgs/week from 35,000
note: Residential per-package tiers for the 2021 holiday window not captured. One source cites an extra $0.60 residential charge from Jan 17, 2022; unverified.

headline: SmartPost rebranded FedEx Ground Economy after last-mile moved off USPS
details: FedEx said it completed integration of last-mile delivery formerly handled by USPS and rebranded SmartPost as FedEx Ground Economy
USPS still delivers some destinations (P.O. boxes, U.S. territories, military mail)
note: Occurred March 2021 (FreightWaves: 'Wednesday'); exact date not confirmed. No direct price change tied to it found.

headline: FedEx raises ongoing peak surcharges: residential, Ground Economy, AHS
details: Residential (domestic air and ground, high-volume shippers): $0.30 to $0.60 per package
Ground Economy (ex-SmartPost): $0.75 to $1.00 per package
Additional Handling: $3.00 to $3.50 per package
Until further notice
note: Residential threshold reported by Lojistic as >30,000 pkgs/week avg in Jan 4-31, 2021; not independently confirmed. Announcement date not confirmed.

headline: U.S. parcel volume hits record 21.5 billion in 2021
details: Pitney Bowes index: 21.5B parcels in 2021, +6% from ~20.3B in 2020
2022 volume roughly flat at ~21.5B
why: Growth slowed sharply after 2020, ending the capacity crunch and shifting leverage back toward shippers.
note: 2020 is restated as 20.3B in this release vs 20.2B earlier. 2022 figure (21.5B) comes from the 2023 index release.

headline: LaserShip and OnTrac agree to merge into a national e-commerce last-mile carrier
details: Definitive agreement announced October 2021; LaserShip owned by American Securities and Greenbriar
Price ~ $1.3B per Moody's (cited by Logistics Management)
Expected to close Q4 2021; networks linked during 2022
Combined company later rebranded under the OnTrac name
why: Created the first coast-to-coast alternative ground carrier for residential e-commerce parcels.
note: Exact close date not verified. Rebrand to OnTrac reported as April 2023 by one company profile only; OnTrac's own announcement page could not be fetched, so rebrand date is unconfirmed.

headline: UPS agrees to acquire Roadie, a crowdsourced same-day delivery platform
details: Announced Sept 10, 2021; terms not disclosed
Roadie runs as a separate wholly owned subsidiary outside the UPS network
~200,000 drivers covering 20,000+ ZIP codes at announcement
Deal closed October 2021 per Roadie
why: Gave UPS a same-day, non-conveyable delivery option outside its core network.
note: Exact close date in October 2021 not verified.

headline: UPS raises domestic air and ground fuel surcharge tables 1 point
details: +1 percentage point on U.S. air and ground fuel surcharges, effective Nov 15, 2021
Followed a +0.75 point table increase effective Aug 16, 2021
note: Single trade source. Not confirmed against UPS fuel tables.

headline: UPS 2021 GRI: 4.9% average net on Ground, Air and International
details: Average net 4.9% for Ground, Air and International, effective Dec 27, 2020 (UPS 10-K)
Analysts: increases weighted toward low-weight Ground and high-zone Air packages
New SurePost rates effective Dec 27, 2020
note: Announced late October 2020. Exact date not confirmed.

headline: UPS 2021 peak: AHS $6, LPS $60, OML $250; residential $1.15-$6.15
details: Oct 3, 2021 - Jan 15, 2022: Additional Handling $6, Large Package $60, Over Maximum Limits $250 per package
Residential Oct 31, 2021 - Jan 15, 2022 for shippers >25,000 pkgs/week after Feb 2020
Ground Residential and SurePost $1.15-$5.15; Air Residential $2.15-$6.15 across five volume tiers
note: Announcement date not confirmed. Figures are from trade press, not the UPS notice.

headline: UPS raises Additional Handling to $3.50 and Large Package peak to $40
details: Additional Handling surcharge $3.00 -> $3.50 per package, effective July 4, 2021
Large Package surcharge $31.45 -> $40 per package, effective July 4, 2021
note: One source gives the prior LPS as $31.50.

headline: USPS unveils 10-year 'Delivering for America' plan
details: Aims to avoid a projected $160B loss over 10 years and reach break-even operating performance
$40B investment in workforce, vehicles, facilities, technology
Keeps six-day mail, expands seven-day package delivery; 13 focus areas, 175 initiatives
why: Set the course for USPS network consolidation, slower service standards and repeated price increases.

headline: 2021 peak surcharge, commercial and retail parcels, Oct 3 - Dec 26, 2021
details: Ran Oct 3 to Dec 26, 2021; first year retail also included
Products: Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, FCPS, Parcel Select, USPS Retail Ground, Parcel Return Service
PM/PME Flat Rate: +$0.75; FCPS: +$0.30; Parcel Return Service: +$1.00
Federal Register: Priority Mail avg +5.7%, Priority Mail Express avg +2.3% during peak
note: Dollar amounts are as filed (EasyPost/Post & Parcel summaries of the USPS filing); PRC approval reported by Logistics Management, but final approved table not separately checked.

headline: January 2021 price change: Priority Mail +3.5%, Priority Mail Express +1.2%
details: Priority Mail: ~+3.5% (USPS)
Priority Mail Express: ~+1.2% (USPS)
USPS noted no surcharges for fuel, residential delivery or regular Saturday delivery
note: Announcement date taken from the USPS newsroom URL (1116); a trade source says competitive prices were filed in November 2020. Other product averages are secondary only and vary by price basis: FCPS +6.2% (eBay summary) / +6.5% Commercial Base (Endicia); Parcel Select +8.9% (eBay) vs Parcel Select Ground +1.3% (Endicia); Retail Ground +3.0% (eBay). Endicia also reports a $100 surcharge for packages over 70 lb or 130 in length+girth; not verified.

headline: Amazon pauses Amazon Shipping for third-party shippers amid pandemic volume surge
details: WSJ/Reuters reported ~Apr 7, 2020 that the service would pause starting June 2020
Capacity redirected to Amazon's own surging customer orders
UPS and FedEx shares rose ~2% after hours on the news
why: Removed a low-cost alternative for shippers exactly when carrier capacity was tightest.
note: Date is the reported start of the pause; announcement was early April 2020.

headline: FedEx 2020 GRI: 4.9% Express/Ground/Home Delivery, 5.9% Freight
details: Express domestic/export/import: avg 4.9%
Ground and Home Delivery: avg 4.9%
FedEx Freight: avg 5.9% (U.S. and certain cross-border lanes)
SmartPost rates increased; percentage not stated
note: One compilation says further surcharge changes effective Jan 20, 2020; single source, not included as fact.

headline: 2020 peak: volume-based residential $1-$5 and SmartPost $1-$2 surcharges
details: Surcharges begin as early as Oct 5, 2020
Residential (Nov 2, 2020 - Jan 17, 2021): $1 to $5 per package for shippers with >=35,000 weekly Ground/Express pkgs, scaled by volume vs pre-pandemic baseline
SmartPost: three tiers from $1 to $2 per package during peak (vs $0.40 since June 8)
Peak oversize reported at $52.50
note: Announced mid-Aug 2020 (Supply Chain Dive, Aug 18, 2020 article says 'Tuesday'); exact date not confirmed. Peak AHS amount not captured.

headline: FedEx adds COVID-era peak surcharges on residential, SmartPost, oversize
details: SmartPost: $0.40 per package
Residential (Express + Ground): $0.30/pkg for enterprise shippers with >=40,000 residential pkgs/week above 120% of Feb 2020 weekly average
Oversize U.S. Express/Ground: $30 per package
In effect until further notice
note: Announced ~June 2-3, 2020; exact date not confirmed. Retail Dive words the residential trigger as 'or' vs 'and' elsewhere. Additional handling peak amount not confirmed.

headline: UPS and FedEx impose pandemic peak surcharges on high-volume residential shippers
details: Surcharges announced at multiple points in 2020 as networks filled
UPS residential peak surcharge applied to shippers over 25,000 parcels/week; FedEx used ~30,000-35,000/week thresholds
Both measured volume growth against February 2020 baselines
FedEx lowered its residential threshold to 25,000/week for 2021
why: Turned temporary surcharges into a lasting cost layer; large e-commerce shippers paid most.
note: Specific thresholds and fee amounts changed repeatedly; check carrier rate notices for exact figures and effective dates.

headline: Pandemic e-commerce surge: U.S. parcel volume jumps 37% to ~20.2 billion
details: Pitney Bowes Parcel Shipping Index: ~20.2B parcels in 2020 vs ~14.8-15B in 2019 (+37%)
U.S. carrier parcel revenue ~$171B, +29%
Amazon Logistics volume rose 127% to 4.2B, passing FedEx (3.3B) by volume
why: Demand outran network capacity, giving carriers pricing power and setting up surcharges and rate hikes.
note: Pitney Bowes gives 2019 base as 15B in press release and 14.8B in its data table. Annual event; no single date.

headline: UPS 2020 GRI: 4.9% average net; new rebill and prohibited item fees
details: Average net 4.9% for UPS Ground, Air and International, effective Dec 29, 2019
Next Day Air and Next Day Air Saver up 5.2% (PARCEL)
Added a rebill fee and a prohibited item fee, plus other changes to value-added services

headline: UPS COVID-era peak surcharges: $31.45 large package, $0.30 residential
details: Large Package peak surcharge $31.45 per package, all service levels, from May 31, 2020 until further notice
$0.30 per Ground Residential and SurePost package for shippers whose volume exceeded February levels by more than 25,000 packages per week
note: Logistics Management gives $31.20 for the large package charge. $31.45 is used by SCD and FreightWaves.

headline: UPS 2020 holiday peak: $1-$4 residential tiers for large shippers; LPS to $50
details: Residential peak Nov 15, 2020 - Jan 16, 2021 for shippers >25,000 pkgs/week, tiered vs Feb 2020 volume
Ground Residential and SurePost $1 (lowest tier) to $3 (top tier); Air Residential $2 to $4
Large Package peak $31.45 -> $50, Oct 4, 2020 - Jan 16, 2021
Reported: Additional Handling $5 and Over Maximum Limits $250 replaced the May 31 surcharges
note: Residential tiers and LPS $50 have multiple sources. AHS $5 / OML $250 have one secondary source, and their effective date is not separately confirmed.

headline: UPS adds $0.24/package SurePost peak increase matching USPS
details: SurePost rates up $0.24 per package from Oct 18, 2020, mirroring a USPS peak surcharge
note: End date not confirmed.

headline: First USPS holiday peak surcharge: commercial parcels, Oct 18 - Dec 27, 2020
details: Ran Oct 18 to Dec 27, 2020; commercial domestic competitive parcels only, retail unaffected
Products: Priority Mail Express, Priority Mail, First-Class Package Service, Parcel Select, Parcel Return Service
PRC approved Sept 4, 2020 (Order 5673 per trade report)
Reported increases: FCPS +$0.25; Priority Mail +$0.40; Priority Mail Express +$1.50; Parcel Select Ground +$0.40; Parcel Select Lightweight +$0.24
note: Dates and scope confirmed by USPS release. Per-product dollar amounts come from trade summaries (Quadient, ShippingEasy); whether they vary by zone/weight was not confirmed against the USPS table. Supply Chain Dive describes 2020 as the start of USPS peak surcharges.

headline: January 2020 price change: Priority Mail +4.1%, Priority Mail Express +3.5%
details: Priority Mail: +4.1% average
Priority Mail Express: +3.5% average
Parcel Select Ground 1 lb starting rate $6.84 to $6.92 (Stamps.com guide)
note: Trade sources report other averages on different bases (EasyPost: Priority Mail +2.8%, Parcel Select Ground +2.5%); USPS figures used. FCPS average not found.

headline: FedEx ends U.S. ground delivery contract with Amazon, after dropping express air deal
details: Announced Aug 7, 2019; ground contract lapsed end of August 2019
Followed FedEx's June 2019 decision not to renew its U.S. Express air contract with Amazon
Amazon was ~1.3% of FedEx 2018 revenue
International agreements continued
why: Marked Amazon's shift from customer to competitor and pushed more Amazon volume to UPS, USPS and Amazon's own network.
note: Exact date of the June 2019 air non-renewal not separately verified.

headline: FedEx mid-year fuel surcharge table increase (not pre-announced)
details: TransImpact reported a fuel surcharge table increase effective Mar 18, 2019, not pre-announced by FedEx
Coincides with end of the Sept 10, 2018 - Mar 17, 2019 table validity on FedEx's PDF
note: Size of change not confirmed; single secondary source plus FedEx table end date.

headline: FedEx 2019 GRI: 4.9% Express/Ground/Home Delivery, 5.9% Freight
details: Express U.S. domestic/export/import: avg 4.9%
Ground and Home Delivery: avg 4.9%
FedEx Freight: avg 5.9%
SmartPost rates also rose; magnitude not disclosed
Oversize Charge $80 to $90; Express Freight surcharge $140 to $175 per handling unit; FreightWaves: fees raised on 56 accessorials
Fortune: FedEx cited fuel costs ~40% higher year over year
note: Unusually late announcement (November vs. September in other years).

headline: FedEx Ground announces year-round 7-day residential delivery and SmartPost insourcing
details: 7-day residential delivery year-round for most of U.S. population starting January 2020
Nearly 2 million daily SmartPost packages previously handed to USPS to be integrated into FedEx Ground
SmartPost was later rebranded FedEx Ground Economy
why: Reduced FedEx reliance on USPS for economy residential parcels and expanded weekend delivery options.
note: Date of SmartPost -> Ground Economy rebrand not verified (FreightWaves reported completion, page could not be fetched). Separately, USPS stopped accepting FedEx Ground Economy drop-offs effective 2024-07-14 (ecommercebytes). Whether/when USPS final-mile delivery of Ground Economy fully ended could not be confirmed; secondary sources conflict (Oct 2024 vs Oct 2025).

headline: 2019 peak: no residential surcharge; higher AHS, oversize peak add-ons
details: FedEx announced no additional residential peak surcharges for third straight holiday season
Peak Additional Handling (Ground): $3.20 to $4.10
Peak Oversize: $27.50 to $37.50
Announced alongside 2020 GRI on Sept 16, 2019
note: Window conflict: one source gives Oct 21, 2019 - Jan 5, 2020; another gives Nov 8, 2019 - Jan 5, 2020 for AHS. Unauthorized peak amount not confirmed (conflicting figures).

headline: UPS 2019 GRI: 4.9% average on Ground, Air and International, on short notice
details: Average 4.9% for UPS Ground, UPS Air and International, effective Dec 26, 2018
About 3 weeks' notice; trade press noted many contracts require 30 days
UPS accessorial notice: Ground Residential Surcharge +$0.35; Over Maximum Limits +$200
Analysts: SurePost rose by as much as 9.3%
note: Announcement date of Dec 5, 2018 is from PARCEL ('yesterday'). UPS's accessorial PDF is labeled 'December 5, 2018 Update'. Air Freight effective date conflicts: Dec 26 (Logistics Management) vs Dec 27 (PARCEL).

headline: UPS drops residential peak surcharges for 2019; AHS/LPS/OML peak fees kept
details: Aug 16, 2019: UPS said no peak surcharges on residential deliveries for 2019 holiday season
Peak surcharges on Additional Handling, Large Package and Over Maximum Limits remained
PARCEL: the three remaining peak charges ranged from an additional $3.60 to $435 per package
note: Per-surcharge 2019 peak amounts and effective windows not confirmed.

headline: Dimensional weight extended to all zones; DIM divisor cut from 194 to 166
details: Priority Mail parcels over 1 cubic foot (1,728 cu in) priced at greater of actual or DIM weight in Zones 1-9 (previously Zones 5-9 only)
DIM divisor reduced from 194 to 166
Priority Mail Express DIM uses divisor 166 (rectangular and nonrectangular formulas)
Parcel Select Ground and Destination Entry: DIM applies to all zones and entries, divisor 166
note: Mid-year structural change (not a list-price change). Announcement date not pinned down; it was published in Postal Bulletin 22509 (2018) as a deferral from January 27, 2019.

headline: January 2019 price change: Priority Mail +5.9%, Priority Mail Express +3.9%
details: Priority Mail: +5.9% average
Priority Mail Express: +3.9% average
First-Class Package Service moved to zone-based pricing
'Balloon' pricing eliminated for Priority Mail zones 1-4 and commercial Parcel Select
Mailing Services ~+2.5%; Forever stamp 50c to 55c
note: pct null: USPS gave no single shipping-wide average. FCPS, Parcel Select and Retail Ground averages not found. New DIM provisions were deferred to June 23, 2019 (see separate entry).

headline: Amazon reported to launch 'Shipping with Amazon' delivery service for businesses, starting in LA
details: WSJ reported Feb 9, 2018; rollout to begin in Los Angeles with third-party marketplace sellers
Amazon drivers pick up from businesses; USPS/other carriers used outside Amazon's reach
Framed as undercutting UPS and FedEx on price
why: First sign Amazon would sell its own last-mile capacity to shippers, competing with UPS/FedEx.
note: Based on WSJ report of a plan; exact first-shipment date not verified.

headline: FedEx updates Express and Ground fuel surcharge tables
details: New Express (jet fuel) and Ground (diesel) tables effective Sept 10, 2018; FedEx PDF lists validity Sept 10, 2018 to Mar 17, 2019
FedEx newsroom said details would be on fedex.com by Aug 10, 2018
AFS: change brought FedEx roughly to parity with UPS fuel tables; FedEx previously 1-5 pts lower on several services
note: Exact percentage-point change by index band not captured. Announcement was in the early-Aug 2018 newsroom release; exact day not confirmed.

headline: FedEx 2018 GRI: 4.9% average for Express, Ground, Home Delivery and Freight
details: Express U.S. domestic/export/import: avg 4.9%; FedEx One Rate avg 3.5%
Ground and Home Delivery: avg 4.9%
FedEx Freight: avg 4.9%
Residential Delivery Charge up 7.8% to $4.15; Oversize Charge up 10.3% to $80; Additional Handling up 9.1% to $12 (per ShipStation analysis)
Jan 22, 2018: new 2.5% Third Party Billing Surcharge (Express, Ground); 139 DIM divisor extended to SmartPost; FedEx Freight Over Length Surcharge $85 (8 ft to <12 ft)
note: Surcharge dollar figures are from secondary analyses (ShipStation/Shipware), not checked against the FedEx service guide. Express/Ground 139 DIM divisor dates from Jan 2, 2017, not this GRI.

headline: 2018 peak: no residential peak surcharge; AHS, oversize, unauthorized add-ons apply
details: Window Nov 19 - Dec 24, 2018
Peak Additional Handling: +$3.20/pkg (U.S. Express, U.S. and international Ground)
Peak Oversize: +$27.50/pkg
Peak Unauthorized package (Ground): +$150/pkg
No additional residential peak surcharges for second straight holiday season
note: Announced early Aug 2018 (Reuters: 'on Friday'); exact day not confirmed so null. One Etsy page lists AHS add-on as $3.30; $3.20 is the better-supported figure.

headline: FedEx raises Additional Handling (weight) and Ground unauthorized package charges
details: Additional Handling - Weight: $12.00 to $20.00
Ground Unauthorized (oversize/over max) package charge: $300 to $675
Described as aligning FedEx with UPS surcharges introduced June-July 2018
note: Two secondary sources (consultancy/software vendor), no FedEx primary or trade press located. Announcement date not confirmed (FedEx newsroom Aug 2018 release referenced changes).

headline: UPS 2018 GRI: 4.9% average net increase on Ground, Air and International
details: Average net 4.9% for UPS Ground, UPS Air and international services, effective Dec 24, 2017
UPS Air Freight (U.S./Canada/Puerto Rico) and UPS Freight LTL tariff 580 also +4.9% average net
Trade press: DIM divisor for packages <=1 cu ft moved from 166 to 139 for Daily Rates (139 already applied to >1 cu ft from Jan 8, 2017)
note: Announcement date and effective date from UPS FY2017 10-K. Exact effective date of the <=1 cu ft DIM divisor change not confirmed.

headline: UPS 2018 peak: $0.28 Ground / $0.99 Air residential; large package and AHS add-ons
details: Residential peak surcharge: $0.28 Ground, $0.99 Air
Large Package peak add-on $26.20 per package, Nov 18 - Dec 22, 2018 (on top of standard LPS)
Additional Handling peak add-on $3.15 per package, Nov 18 - Dec 22, 2018
note: Residential amounts have two sources. LPS/AHS add-ons and the Nov 18 - Dec 22 window come from PARCEL only. Announcement date and residential windows not confirmed.

headline: UPS raises Over Maximum Limits and oversize pallet charges, adds audit fee
details: Over Maximum Limits and Oversize Pallet Handling surcharges increased June 4, 2018
Shipping charge correction audit fee introduced
note: New charge amounts not confirmed.

headline: UPS adds residential Large Package and >70 lb Additional Handling surcharges
details: U.S. residential Large Package Surcharge introduced July 8, 2018 (reported at $90)
Additional Handling surcharge for packages over 70 lb introduced (reported at $19)
note: Dollar amounts come from a search summary of UPS 10-Q/10-K text, not read directly. Check before display.

headline: January 2018 general price change: most shipping products up ~3.9% on average
details: Most Shipping Services products: +3.9% average (USPS)
Priority Mail: +3.9% overall; retail +0.8%; Commercial Base +6.2% (Federal Register)
Priority Mail Express: +3.9% overall
Mailing Services (letter mail) ~+1.9%; Forever stamp 49c to 50c
note: First-Class Package Service and Parcel Select product averages not verified from a primary source (a ProShip blog claims Parcel Select +4.9% / +7% for <=1 lb; not used). PRC docket number not retrieved. No peak surcharge existed in 2018; USPS peak pricing began in 2020.
